source: Northcraft et al. (1998), Tables 1–2 and Methods, printed pp. 66–67. https://doi.org/10.1006/obhd.1998.2750
explanation: Every issue has nonnegative payoffs. The unprinted scaled issues also have nonnegative endpoints and the stated positive preference function. The instructions explicitly give zero for impasse. Therefore every complete offer meets both thresholds.
controls_source: Northcraft et al. (1998), Experimental Materials, printed p. 66 / PDF p. 13: Applicant and Recruiter negotiate six five-option issues: four integrative, one distributive, one congruent.

strict_boundary.congruent_step_proof: All source-family payoffs are nonnegative. The printed congruent issue gives both roles zero only at E and gives both roles positive points at A-D. A zero-total party therefore requires congruent E; changing that issue alone to A gives both roles positive totals and increases the approval count to agreement.
strict_boundary.assumption: The two unprinted integrative issues retain the described strictly monotone, zero-based scaled preference shape, with exactly one zero-payoff option per role per issue. Their complete numerical arrays and physical-name mapping are not recovered. This structural inference is used only as an explicit main-calculation assumption; it does not establish strict-evidence eligibility.
